chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: When one of you buys meat, let him remove the glands from it, for indeed it stirs up the vein of leprosy.

key_terms.الجذام: Leprosy (judhaam) — a severe skin disease feared in classical Islamic society
key_terms.الغدد: Glands/lymph nodes — lymphatic tissue found throughout the body of animals, considered undesirable in food
key_terms.عرق الجذام: The vein/root of leprosy — the underlying cause or latent factor of leprosy that can be activated

ai.seo_question: Should glands be removed from meat before eating according to Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a directive from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the preparation of meat: the lymph nodes and glands must be removed before consumption. The reason given is that leaving these in the meat activates or aggravates the root cause of leprosy (al-judhaam). This represents classical Islamic medical ethics where the Imams provided guidance at the intersection of dietary law and preventive health.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Al Asamma, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When one of you buys meat, so he should extract the glands from it, for it stirs the vein of leprosy’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn al-Shammun from al-Asamm from Misma‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If anyone of you buys meat, he must take out the glands because it accelerates the vein of leprosy.’”
